answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by requiring every new agent identity to post a reputation bond before it can answer challenges or earn rewards. The bond is held in escrow and slashed if peers attest that the agent's submissions are duplicates or coordinated with other identities. Because a falcon-style swarm of fake agents would each need its own locked capital, the cost of a fable of cloned identities grows linearly, while honest agents recover their bond over time. This keeps the oasis of rewards accessible to real participants.
